title: Verify jit-project-lead skeleton activation and evals
description:
Confirm the jit-project-lead skeleton activates correctly from its own description and passes scenario evals scoped to the skeleton's shell and tier-derivation behavior, using the eval adjudication method already established for the other lead skills.

## Background

`jit-execution-lead` and `jit-planning-lead` each carry a scenario-eval suite and an adjudication method for judging trigger accuracy and pass/fail; that method is assumed already in place ahead of this task. Since this story delivers only the orchestrator shell and tier derivation (no mode-routing block or mode bodies), the evals in scope here cover activation and derivation only: whether a representative request activates jit-project-lead, and whether the tier derivation produces the correct steward anchor and delegation boundary for this repository's ruleset and for the collapsed `docs/examples/research` ruleset.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A trigger-eval check confirms jit-project-lead activates from its `SKILL.md` `description` field for representative project-lead-level requests, and does not spuriously activate for requests scoped to `jit-execution-lead` or `jit-planning-lead`.
- [hard] REQ-02: An eval scenario file for jit-project-lead exists (mirroring the shape of `.claude/skills/jit-execution-lead/evals/evals.json`) with scenarios covering: activation, tier derivation against this repository's config, tier derivation against `docs/examples/research/config.toml`, and the stop-and-ask fallback path.
- [hard] REQ-03: Running the established eval procedure against jit-project-lead's scenario file records a pass for every scenario in scope.

## Notes

This task exercises the skeleton only; scenarios requiring the mode-routing block or mode bodies belong to follow-up stories and are out of scope here.
